newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - spot market subdued.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - spot market subdued.

text.p: Spot business on the New York physical coffee market remained sparce this week, but dealers said the pace of producer selling picked up as CSCE futures slid to one-month lows.
"There was a fair amount of price fixing," one dealer said. "Roasters are taking advantage of the sell-off to price coffee from 110 (cents a lb basis CSCE December) down."

While prompt supplies of mild coffees were still tight, underpinning spot differentials, dealers said spreads on coffees for forward delivery eased ahead of the upcoming Colombian and Central American harvests.
"The forward prices reflect that shippers will have a lot of coffee," another dealer said. "The anticipated availability of coffee has brought down the price."

Premiums for Colombian beans for delivery toward the end of 1996 continued to drift lower this week. Colombian MAMs for first-half November delivery were heard done at 16.75 cents over the December contract, down from 19 cents over for November-December delivery last week.
But with many spot beans in short supply, Brazilian coffees continued to fill the void.
